# Independent productive-pool forcing and profile-obstruction review

30 October 2026. Frozen copies in `product_sources/`:
- PRODUCTIVE_POOL_FORCING.md: e07631aa6157cd164a8be52a783945aaf251ac75100521a88c7be355c211b61d.
- PRODUCTIVE_POOL_PROFILE_OBSTRUCTION.md: 6b5926245f2bbb038a17b2500ace97b1257447399a83ad16776a75e12dccd61c.

**Verdict: accept the deterministic-time productive-pool forcing theorem and the exact obstruction to a population-uniform A-only incoming inverse-profile bound.** The candidate carried martingale is valid but is not a completed inverse-profile barrier, Green theorem or global transfer.

## Forcing

When initial Y>=n/2, a selected persistent working cohort has uniformly bounded adverse participation for the whole horizon by monotonicity of Y. The reviewed product theorem therefore supplies the stronger nT^L scale, which implies the weaker claimed scale for T<=1 after constants are reduced.

Otherwise at least n/2 initial identities are source labels. Genuine disjoint entry subrates admit independent rate-gamma potential clocks for those identities. A clock ring by the midpoint ensures that identity is already working, even if an extra entry occurred first. This proves the binomial domination, not independence of the realized worker population. It requires irreversible source membership and the explicitly genuine allocation; one shared conversion event cannot be credited repeatedly.

On first-half success, choose an integer cohort M of order nT from actual midpoint workers. Their membership persists and the denominator 1+Y cannot decrease. Their adverse participation is at most B/T throughout the remaining horizon, even when source-entry events cause adverse collateral resets. All such participation was required to be counted. The product damping exp(-constant b_T T) is consequently bounded below uniformly; the Poisson rank-progress factor contributes T^L. Conditional application of the genuine progress generator gives threshold and exponent of order nT^(L+1). No successful future-rank or survival conditioning occurs. For small nT the prefactor K can cover the bounded exponent, including integer-cohort issues.

## Exact dilution mechanism

The obstruction has fixed n, irreversible source entries, and exactly one existing worker reset uniformly per entry. Its per-worker adverse participation gamma C/Y is at most 2 gamma C/(1+Y) for Y>=1;

# Productive-pool forcing despite an initially unbounded C/Y reset rate

30 October 2026. New local candidate. This is a resource-consuming pool mechanism, not an additional named chemical network or an integrated theorem.

There are n persistent labels divided into a source pool C and a working pool W, size Y=n-C. Working labels have ranks0,...,L, L>=1; rank0 is target. Source labels are not targets. Assume:

1. Source membership is irreversible during the episode. Each source label has a genuinely allocated entry subrate gamma>0 converting it to a working label of rank<=L. Extra conversions may help. Allocated physical rates are not double-counted.
2. Each working label has genuinely allocated rank-progress subrate q>0, with designated rank decreasing by at least1 and any collateral working changes safe.
3. Other working-rank changes are safe or adverse. Each adverse event touches at most k EXISTING working labels, and each working label's total adverse participation intensity is bounded by

       b0+b1 C/(1+Y).

   A source-entry event may also cause such an adverse batch; its actual participation is included in this bound. New labels from C are not part of a previously selected working cohort.
4. The exact process is nonexplosive and all generator allocations use the same clock. No births, deletions, or return from W to C occurs in this local statement.

Then there are constants c,K>0 such that for0<T<=1,

    P(A_T<c n T^(L+1))<=K exp[-c n T^(L+1)],         (P)

uniformly in the initial pool/rank configuration. In particular the initial adverse bound may be of order n when Y is small; no uniform initial per-label bound or small return norm is assumed.

## Proof

If initially Y>=n/2, select a working cohort of size floor(n/2). Monotonicity keeps Y>=n/2, so its adverse participation is bounded by b0+2b1 throughout. The root product theorem yields the stronger threshold/order n T^L. This implies (P) after adjusting constants, including small n.

# Productive dilution defeats an A-only incoming profile

30 October 2026. Exact abstract local obstruction, not a counterexample to earlier fixed-rate or birth/seed theorems.

Fix q,gamma,kappa>0 and integer killing degree m>=1. There are n labels. Source C enters the working pool at rate gamma per source label. Each entry creates one working rank1 label AND chooses one of the previous Y working labels uniformly, resetting that label to rank1. (If Y=0, no reset is made.) Every working rank1 label progresses independently to target rank0 at rate q. Thus each existing working label has adverse participation gamma C/Y, batch size1. For Y>=1 this is <=2 gamma C/(1+Y), so PRODUCTIVE_POOL_FORCING applies. Kill at rate kappa(A)_m.

Take initial Y=A=a_n=floor(n^epsilon), all initially working labels target, with

    0<epsilon<min{1/4,1/(m+1)}.

Set T_n=a_n^2/n, which tends to zero. Let the comparison process suppress all working progress until T_n. Its working population is

    Y_t=a_n+Binomial(n-a_n,1-exp(-gamma t)),

independent of which labels the entry resets select. Write Z_t for the initially-target labels not yet reset. Conditional on Y_t=y, each growth step at working size r preserves a given old target with probability1-1/r. Therefore

    E[Z_t |Y_t=y]=a_n(a_n-1)/(y-1).

More generally, for a fixed j<=a_n-1,

    E[(Z_t)_j |Y_t=y]
       =(a_n)_j (a_n-1)_j/(y-1)_j.                 (D)

This follows because j distinct specified old labels all avoid one reset with probability1-j/r, and the product telescopes as r runs from a_n to y-1. It is not independent survival of the old targets.

At T_n the binomial mean is of order a_n^2. A lower-tail Chernoff bound in (D), first for j=1, gives E Z_(T_n)<=C uniformly in n. In contrast the incoming inverse profile is f_s(A_0)=(1+a_n)^(-s)->0.

The probability that ANY working progress occurs by T_n is at most

    q E integral_0^T_n Y_t dt
       <=q[a_n T_n+gamma n T_n^2/2]
       =O(a_n^3/n+a_n^4/n)->0.

Thus the comparison agrees with the actual target dynamics up to T_n with probability tending to1.

The kill also occurs before T_n with probability tending to0. Indeed pay the preceding progress event separately; otherwise its hazard is kappa(Z_t)_m. For t<=a_n/n, use (Z_t)_m<=a_n^m. For a_n/n<t<=T_n, binomial concentration and (D) give the integral bound

    E integral_0^T_n (Z_t)_m dt
       <= C a_n^(m+1)/n +
